entries.what_happened: The manuscript 'A counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture' (OpenAI, dated September 23, 2026) is the only manuscript in this family. It claims one bipartite graph H on 35 vertices and 66 edges, and a finite simple graph G with at least one edge, such that t(H,G) < p(G)⁶⁶. Here t(H,G) is the homomorphism density (non-injective maps counted, normalised by |V(G)|^|V(H)|) and p(G) = 2|E(G)|/|V(G)|² is the edge density. H is the incidence graph of 22 triples on 13 points, listed explicitly in Table 'tab:complex' (sections/complex.tex); it is connected, with parts of size 13 and 22, degrees 4, 5 and 6 on the point side and 3 on the face side. The argument has three steps. (1) A finite symmetric [0,1]-valued kernel U with mean μ > 0 and t(H,U) < μ⁶⁶ is built from a rectangular kernel over random symmetric matrices over F_q, symmetrised by a crossed product and diluted (Proposition 'negative-kernel', sections/kernel.tex). (2) That step is conditional on the rank-layer limit, Lemma 'Rank-layer limit', which the manuscript proves in its own Sections 3 to 6. (3) A finite simple host G on n vertices is sampled from U, with n > (595 + 66μ⁶⁶)/Δ and Δ = μ⁶⁶ − t(H,U) (Lemma 'finite-host'). The same manuscript also refutes the graphon form: the {0,1} adjacency kernel W₀ of G on the uniform measure on V(G) has t(K₂,W₀) = p(G) and t(H,W₀) = t(H,G) < p(G)⁶⁶ (proof of Corollary 'Failure of the forcing conjecture', sections/consequences.tex). The manuscript also claims, for this same H, a failure of the Conlon–Fox–Sudakov forcing conjecture and amplification and injective-copy results. Those are not matched problems here and are not described further.
entries.delivers: Disproves Sidorenko's conjecture as the list states it. The conjecture quantifies over every bipartite graph H, so a single bipartite H with t(H,W) < t(K₂,W)^{e(H)} for some graphon W refutes the universal claim. The counterexample is for this one graph, which is connected, bipartite and has 35 vertices and 66 edges. It is given in the finite-graph form (a finite simple host G with at least one edge). The graphon form in the list is also refuted, by the step graphon W₀ of G, since t(K₂,W₀) = p(G) and t(H,W₀) = t(H,G). The manuscript's own statement (its displayed inequality, with p(G) = 2|E|/|V|² for finite simple G, and 'bipartite with at least one edge') matches the list's statement up to the finite-graph versus graphon wording, which W₀ bridges. The manuscript says 'We disprove this conjecture', so it claims a full negative answer to the universal statement, not a partial or sharpened one. The manuscript also notes that H has no vertex adjacent to the whole opposite part, is not weakly norming (its point-side degrees are not regular), and fails the degree-count hypotheses of the positive results it cites. So it does not contradict those positive theorems, which concern other graphs.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, the universal statement as frozen is false and nothing of it remains open. Not addressed: which bipartite graphs do satisfy the inequality, beyond the positive classes already known; whether H is minimal in size or edge count; and whether any local or restricted version holds for H (the manuscript says the local kernel results of Lovász do not apply to its kernel). The host G is given only by existence, not explicitly.
entries.direction: disproves the conjecture (one bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges)
entries.object: H is explicit: the incidence graph of 22 triples on 13 points, all triples written out in Table 'tab:complex' (sections/complex.tex). The host G is not explicit. It is produced by a probabilistic sampling argument from a finite kernel, after choosing a large fixed even dimension D, a small ε > 0 and a large odd prime q, each chosen only as 'sufficiently large' or 'sufficiently small'. The manuscript does not write G down and does not give its order beyond the existential bound n > (595 + 66μ⁶⁶)/Δ, where Δ depends on the constructed kernel.
entries.conditional_on: No external unproven hypothesis is stated for the Sidorenko disproof. Internally, the finite kernel (Proposition 'negative-kernel') and the host lemma are proved conditional on Lemma 'Rank-layer limit' (kernel.tex). The manuscript proves that lemma itself in Sections 3 to 6 (transverse, orbits, planted, tail), so the dependence is internal rather than on another paper. The sampling step follows the standard graphon sampling construction of Lovász and Szegedy (Section 2.6, Lemma 2.4) and gives its own collision bound. Standard inputs used without re-proof are the quadratic Gauss-sum rank bound (Gowers–Wolf, Lemma 3.3), the association-scheme counts of symmetric matrices by rank and sign (Huo–Wan; Schmidt), the Lagrangian counting formulas (Taylor), and the colour-refinement facts (Weisfeiler–Leman; McKay).
entries.doubts: (1) The rank-layer lemma carries the whole result. Its proof spans about 2,400 lines (Sections 3 to 6). I read its statement, the assembly at the end of tail.tex, and the passages flagged here, not the full proof. (2) The singular-contribution proposition (tail.tex, 'Vanishing singular contribution') bounds the local maximising tuples only by necessary dimension inequalities. The text says these 'need not be realizable simultaneously', so the bound is an upper bound by design. (3) The numerical remainder 1641 and the requirement D > 1641 (tail.tex, 'Costs for the remaining profiles' and the singular-contribution proof) are asserted. The text says D > 1641 'is needed here only for the nondirect residual case and is not asserted to be a threshold for the whole proof'. I did not check the derivation of 1641. (4) The choice of D, ε and q is non-quantitative throughout, so the existence of G is not quantified. (5) In the rank-layer proof, the comparison that drops the prescribed signs off the transverse set is dismissed in one sentence: 'dropping the prescribed signs only enlarges the integrand after the comparable normalizations'. (6) The finite-host proof calls the probability that a map is a homomorphism a 'homomorphism indicator between zero and one'. The quantity is a probability; the collision bound is unaffected. (7) The abstract, the displayed theorem and the corollary statements agree on 35 vertices, 66 edges and a strict inequality for a finite simple graph with at least one edge.
